title: Design exercise: SAA-2.1-S02
scenario: Pinecrest Tutoring runs a live-lesson web tier that normally serves about 1,500 requests per second but reaches 4,000 every weekday when schools finish. The peak start shifts by up to an hour from week to week with term calendars that nobody at Pinecrest tracks. A new server needs roughly 10 minutes before it can take traffic, and in September students saw errors during the first 8 minutes of each peak. On top of the peak, unannounced surges of up to 30 percent occur whenever a teacher assigns a live quiz, and holding peak capacity around the clock would break the monthly compute cap.
constraints: Do not claim live AWS experience
There is no on-call rota, and engineers must not hand-edit timetables when school calendars change
Monthly compute spend is capped at 2,500 USD

rubric.label: Capacity is in place before each peak given the 10-minute warm-up, without a hand-maintained calendar
Unannounced 30 percent surges are absorbed with no manual action and without running peak capacity around the clock

constraint_reason: Mapped as design_exercise to complete skill coverage when no dedicated live lab step exists
